notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/bd9acd99775588a689f7ec1827223fdd5138ba2c.png[/img]

Hello everyone,

We're here with the final status update before the release. We're ready to share the episode, but we've reached a point where the status updates are all pretty much the same. I ran out of things to write about three updates ago.

We've now finished all the scenes and rendered almost all of them. What's left to do is code and polish the script while we wait for the animations to render. This is taking quite a long time, especially with the ones that have 600 frames. So far, we have over 30 animations at 60 fps, each with at least 200 frames.

notes.title: The Grey Dream Episode 7 - Status Update #8
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/0e8324a143198e08189357d6c647d227968492a4.png[/img]
Hello everyone,

This week we've been busy with animations again. But before we get to that, let's talk about why we haven't had a status update for Greyvale Rivalry this week. As you may know, we've said that The Grey Dream will be our priority until we finish this season, so we thought it was only right to shift our full focus to finishing Episode 7 for a few weeks.

Now we can talk about what we've been doing over the last week, we've been rendering animations pretty much non-stop and with all this rushing we've finished 70% of the animations in this episode, not counting the cinematic. With all these animations done, we're getting closer to the release every week. We haven't been lazy on the rendering front either, we've finished 3 more scenes. Overall we're really happy with the progress we've made over the last 2 weeks.

Before we get to the scenes, we've asked you to leave a review on the last status update. We would like to thank everyone who left a review. It has really boosted our morale.

Render-wise, we weren't really focusing on one scene, we were working on the transition renders between the animations. There are about 50 renders.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/6b94c941bcc33d929b1601c33d2691b604042157.png[/img]
Hello there,

We don't really have anything special or personal to share, so let's just get right to it. We've been rendering animations pretty much non-stop for the last 2 weeks. Some nights we've had some problems with our electricity and we've also had some problems with some animations that have cost us a few days, but overall we're in a good place with the development of episode 6.

Since we love to share the numbers, let's get to them. Another 10 animations have been completed. In the last few episodes, the animations were in the 90-120 frame range, but in this episode we have upped our game and pushed them into the 160-270 range. We think they look a lot smoother, but they also take almost twice as long to render. Still, we're very pleased with the results.

As for the renders, we've finished posing and rendering 3 more scenes and started work on another branching scene.

First of all, after we returned from the break, Kagan had the flu and I caught it from him, so we were down for a few days. Anyway, after a few days, we started working on the game and made some progress.

Let's start with the numbers last week we posed and rendered 250 renders but other than that we started the first branching scene of this episode which means that in the next few weeks, we have to start working on the animations and I have to say that the second 4090 will come in handy on the coding side 3 more scenes are fully written and coded and I have to say that one of them was the longest scene we have ever written and now that it is out of the way we can continue working on the usual scenes.

We are also trying out some new things for a possible future project, but since we are not sure if we want to make those things we will keep the details private for now.

notes.title: Episode 6 - Status Update #1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/b82adf5c77af810d11177eab9891d6258df5dff7.png[/img]
Hello there,

We're back. After releasing episode 5 we thought we should take a break, but instead we started working on the next episode. It's at a good point right now, so we're going to work on it for another week and then take a break, and oh boy, do we need that break. We did not take a break while we were making the last episode and we just had so many problems that we were on the verge of burnout, so this break was a lifesaver for us. We're not planning on taking a long break, just a week or so, and then we'll get back to work on the game. But before we take a break, let's talk about what we've been doing the last 2 weeks while working on Episode 6.

So far we've finished 10 scenes with 500 renders. Please don't ask me how Kagan managed to pose and render so much, he wanted to do his absolute best before taking a break, so we are at an excellent point in terms of development for the new chapter. We haven't done anything with the animations yet, they take at least a day to render, so we plan to do them last.

That's about it. Thanks for sticking with us through the last development cycle, we hope you will stick with us through this one too.

notes.title: Episode 5 - Status Update #7
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/883f9be1cb72852a5105919e5ba5aa253966d3e6.png[/img]
Hello everyone,

We are back with another status update. So what has happened in the last two weeks? Let's start with the art part of the game. Except for a few missing renders in some scenes, all static renders are complete. Apart from the static renders, we're still rendering the animations for the final cinematic and some scenes, which takes almost a day each. Writing and coding is also going well. With the current pace of work, it looks like the test version of the game will be ready in the next week or two, and after that we should be good to go for the release of the next episode in July. 

Now that we have the status out of the way, we can talk about why this episode took 6 months to make. It started with the steam release and the tax stuff. To be fair, those things only took 1 month to manage and complete, but after that, when we went back to work on episode 5, we had a problem with our GPU, which we made a post about back then. Anyway, we changed our GPU and went back to development. Now you might be wondering why we bothered to explain this, but we wanted to clarify and maybe justify the long development cycle of this episode. Hopefully now that everything is straightened out, the next dev cycles won't be as long.

We're really sorry for the delay with this status update. We got caught up with some tax stuff and had to take a few days off to sort things out. 

The last few weeks have been all about animations. We mentioned in the previous status updates that we wanted to make the animations longer once we had the adequate systems. Now that we have them, we are putting them to good use with the animations. Currently we've rendered 1500 frames of animation with a quality that we're happy with for now. Besides the animations, the renders are also coming along nicely. We're closing in on another 200 renders and now that the animations are out of the way, we can focus on the renders again.

notes.title: Episode 5 - Status Update #3
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/6c2d188629905fc478a1fc2fc2a059239bf37824.png[/img]
Hello there,

We're back with another status update. The last two weeks have been pretty smooth. We only had an issue with one asset. For some reason the asset couldn't see it's png file and gave us a headache for a few days. We eventually fixed it, but those 3 days were annoying.

Let's talk progress. We've finished another 300 renders of 5 scenes. On the coding side, 4 more scenes are coded and the fifth is on its way.

Anyway, as I was writing this, I realized that 4090 is making things so much faster and we need to share weekly status updates, so we might as well go to a weekly schedule with these updates.

notes.title: Episode 5 - Status Update #2
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/992a861a60cf2cb16ca5fcd8527caeed2c575fdf.png[/img]
Hello there,

We are finally back with another status update. If you read the previous quick check-ins, we had some problems with our GPU and we couldn't solve the problem and we ended up upgrading to the 4090 and wow, this card is something else! 

So what happened this week? We've done about 300 renders with triple the amount of samples. Now that we know what the 4090 can do, rendering animations doesn't seem like such a pain anymore. Also, 300 may seem like half an episode compared to previous episodes, but we wanted to make Episode 5 bigger than usual.

We know we weren't the most active developers last month, but you guys still supported us during that time, so we just want to say thank you again.

notes.title: Episode 5 - Status Update #1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44430369/8fdac811763c13c15f81ad0e5188e04e656b76d3.png[/img]
Hello there,

It's been a little over a week since we released The Grey Dream on Steam, and we'd like to thank everyone who bought it or supported us along the way. Normally we planned to take some time off after the Steam release, but we thought why not work some more on Ep 5? So here we are with the first status update of Episode 5.

Thanks to all of you we are finally able to update our system. With these system upgrades coming up, we decided to just post the renders for now instead of spending days rendering them. This way, once we get the new rigs, we will be able to render faster with more samples.

On the story side, we've decided on the details of the first 5 scenes and have written a few more, but we're still working on their details. And for those who are curious about the story, let's say that your actions will definitely show it's consequences in this episode.
